Chapter 211: All Kinds of Resources at His Disposal

Class ended, and he prepared to leave.

Wan Nannan asked, "Do you want to copy the class notes?"

"I've memorized them," Chen Guiliang said.

For other courses, he might have to borrow a classmate's notes to photocopy for the final exam. But for this class, he really didn't need to. He was sure to pass.

Wan Nannan asked again, "Are you coming tonight?"

"Is there a lecture?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Wan Nannan said, "Tonight at 7, in Guanghua's Room 202 auditorium, Chen Xiaoxu is coming to give a speech. The theme is 'Challenging the Workplace'."

"The one who played Lin Daiyu?" Chen Guiliang said.

Wan Nannan nodded. "That's her."

Chen Guiliang said, "I'll try my best to be there."

"You really are a busy man," Wan Nannan muttered, walking out of the classroom with him.

The guy from the next seat didn't say anything, just quietly followed behind them.

Chen Guiliang followed the other students, moving from the classroom to the entrance of the academic building, where he saw a group of middle-aged men and women.

"What are they here for?" Chen Guiliang asked curiously.

Wan Nannan said, "Probably some kind of professional development program."

The guy from the next seat finally spoke up. "The 15th Term of the Chinese Enterprise Operators Program. There are two classes, A and B, with over 80 people in total."

Peking University's Guanghua School of Management often held various classes. On one hand, to make extra money, and on the other, to develop its network.

Among them, the Guanghua MBA and EMBA programs were the most prestigious, gathering top figures from all industries.

As for the program right in front of them, it was of a much lower tier, and the tuition was far cheaper. The students were basically from medium-sized enterprises, either as owners or senior executives.

An idea sparked in Chen Guiliang's mind.

He could totally pull these people onto Xiaonei and Kaixin. As long as he taught them how to use it, they would definitely become loyal Weibo users!

He couldn't be sure about other things, but if he invited them to join Xiaonei, these people would probably be even more enthusiastic than he was.

Because their little circle on Xiaonei would have the prefix "Peking University Guanghua School of Management Class."

Did they really come to Peking University purely to learn business management knowledge?

Developing connections was also key. And after that, it was for show!

And pulling them into the Peking University class on Xiaonei would allow them to both maintain their connections and show off.

When they returned to their respective companies, they might even proactively promote ByteDance's websites. Especially Kaixin, because their colleagues and subordinates couldn't get into Xiaonei.

Hmm, the MBA and EMBA classes at Peking University's Guanghua School and National School of Development could also be brought onto Xiaonei and Kaixin. The big shots from various fields also had social networking needs!

Why hadn't he thought of this before?

He had forgotten to use the resources right in front of him.

Chen Guiliang called his secretary. "Immediately send someone to deliver 90 sets of Legends of the Three Kingdoms, and also bring a set of my Type B business cards. The address is Guanghua School, 1st floor. Remember, come in through the East Gate. Bring two or three extra people to help me carry those Legends of the Three Kingdoms sets."

At this time, as long as you registered your license plate and purpose at the gate, vehicles from outside could still enter the Peking University campus. The management was very relaxed.

Unlike a few years later, when you would have to make an appointment in advance.

Wan Nannan roughly guessed what he was planning to do and said, amused and exasperated, "CEO Chen, you really seize every single opportunity to develop your business."

"Can't be helped, it's the early stage of the startup," Chen Guiliang said. "If there are any more of these programs in the future, please let me know."

"Sure, but you'll have to treat me to a meal," Wan Nannan said with a smile.

Chen Guiliang said, "No problem, pick any restaurant you want." He glanced at the guy next to him. "Classmate, could you help me keep an eye out as well?"

After all, he was a new internet tycoon. There was no need to be on bad terms; they might be able to help each other someday. The guy thought for a moment, then nodded and said, "Alright."

Only then did Chen Guiliang ask, "May I ask your name?"

The guy was instantly speechless. *I've been in this class with you for a whole semester. And we've been in another class together at Guanghua for a year. That's a full year and a half, and you still don't know my name?*

Forget it.

*Seeing as you often skip class and haven't attended many sessions, I'll be the bigger person and not hold it against you!*

The guy said, "My name is He Weihang."

"Can I get your number?" Chen Guiliang said.

He Weihang took out his phone. "I'll call you. What's your number?"

After they exchanged numbers, Chen Guiliang asked, "Do you play Legends of the Three Kingdoms? I'll give you a set of physical cards."

"You'd better just give me a set of skins," He Weihang said. He was actually an online player.

Chen Guiliang said, "Ten skins, pick any you like."

"I want all five champion skins," He Weihang said.

Chen Guiliang said, "Text me your game ID and the skins you want."

He Weihang, who had been making sour, jealous remarks during class, had now inexplicably become friendly with Chen Guiliang again. It was as if they had been friends all along.

Wan Nannan looked at the two of them. "Is Legends of the Three Kingdoms really that fun?"

"You'll know once you try it," Chen Guiliang said. "I'm having someone bring over 90 sets, I'll give you one."

The three of them found an empty classroom to sit and chat, waiting for the Youke employees to deliver the goods.

As they talked a little more deeply, Chen Guiliang learned that Wan Nannan was a true Beijinger, while He Weihang was from the fashionable "International-zhuang."

About half an hour later, the Jinbei van carrying the Legends of the Three Kingdoms cards arrived. The van parked by the roadside, and a few employees carried boxes of cards into the academic building.

"Move them upstairs," Chen Guiliang directed.

In another two years, the various professional programs run by the Guanghua School would be uniformly arranged on the 2nd floor. But at this time, they often used the classrooms on the 1st floor of Guanghua.

Wan Nannan and He Weihang had only studied theory; they had never seen business being conducted in practice, so they followed along curiously to watch the excitement.

The two program classes were still in session.

Chen Guiliang wasn't in a hurry. He had the employees place the cardboard boxes in the hallway, open them up, and reveal the card game boxes inside.

After waiting another twenty minutes, it seemed Class B was no longer in a formal lesson; a professor was just chatting idly with the students.

Chen Guiliang asked, "What's the surname of the professor in there?"

Wan Nannan took a look and said, "Professor Liu from the Department of Health Economics and Management."

"Is he easy to talk to?" Chen Guiliang asked again.

He Weihang said, "He's quite humorous, can take a joke."

Chen Guiliang walked to the doorway, but didn't go in, just stood there listening to Professor Liu's idle chat.

Professor Liu turned his head, glanced at Chen Guiliang twice, and asked, "Can I help you?"

Chen Guiliang replied, "I just happened to have nothing to do, so I came over to listen to Professor Liu's lecture for the entrepreneurs."

"Then come on in."

Professor Liu smiled and introduced him to the students. "Don't be fooled by how young this student is, he's already a big boss. Last year, he received 5 million US dollars in venture capital, making him worth over a hundred million at just 19."

"Whoa—"

A buzz went through the classroom.

Someone had already recognized Chen Guiliang.

Someone else remembered the news report but had forgotten Chen Guiliang's name.

And some people had never seen the report at all.

These students had an average age of 42. They came from various industries, and there was even a coal boss among them. The relatively weaker ones had companies with annual sales of only forty or fifty million yuan, with a net profit of just two or three million.

Many of the students didn't care about the internet at all and rarely read professional financial magazines.

Professor Liu beckoned. "Come on up and say a few words."

"My apologies for the interruption, Professor Liu," Chen Guiliang said as he walked in.

He Weihang looked at Wan Nannan. "He just went in like that?"

Wan Nannan smiled. "He really knows how to handle things."

Chen Guiliang stood on the podium. "Everyone here is a senior and an elite of the Chinese business world. And Professor Liu is here, a top expert in business management. For a young kid like me, I really wouldn't dare to speak presumptuously. You seniors have come to Peking University for further studies and are probably too busy with your coursework to have much entertainment. I'd like to give you all a gift, something to use for leisure and conversation during your time in Beijing."

With that, Chen Guiliang walked out of the classroom and said to the two people in the hallway, "Could you please lend a hand?"

Wan Nannan and He Weihang were instantly turned into manual laborers, helping Chen Guiliang carry in the Legends of the Three Kingdoms card sets and distribute them.

Chen Guiliang also included a business card for each person—the kind that only had his secretary's phone number.

Professor Liu didn't stop them, watching the three students bustle about with a grin.

As Chen Guiliang handed out his business cards, the students also gave him theirs. In an instant, he received a large stack.

Most of the companies on the cards, he had never even heard of.

After he had handed out most of the games and cards, Chen Guiliang began to introduce his company.

When they heard that only students could register on Xiaonei, and that after registering, they would all be grouped into the "Peking University Guanghua School of Management Class," the students immediately became interested.

Next, he introduced Kaixin, using celebrities like Li Ao, Han Han, and Yu Quan as a hook. Then he hyped up Weibo to the heavens, coaxing the students to activate their mobile Weibo accounts.

In passing, he also invited them to visit ByteDance and Youke.

These students had both time and money, and were particularly willing to make friends with other entrepreneurs. Almost every cohort would organize some kind of project. For example, last year's 14th cohort, a group of students pooled their money to go and renovate a rural school.

"Little brother, are you coming to dinner tonight? We can sing karaoke together!" a coal boss actively invited him.

Chen Guiliang said, "Not tonight. I have to go to Chen Xiaoxu's lecture, the actress who played Lin Daiyu."

"Chen Xiaoxu is giving a lecture at Peking University today?" Immediately, some entrepreneurs wanted to go see their idol.

Chen Guiliang said with a smile, "I'm afraid you seniors won't be able to attend. Only current students can enter the lecture hall. I can pass on everyone's well wishes to Chen Xiaoxu for you."

"Then I'll prepare a small gift, and you can help me deliver it," a male entrepreneur in his 40s said.

"No problem," Chen Guiliang readily agreed.

Chen Guiliang would just have to take on the task of delivering everyone's gifts to Chen Xiaoxu. While he was at it, he would get an autograph and ask if Chen Xiaoxu would be willing to join Kaixin.

After chatting with the group of students for a while, He Weihang stood at the door and coughed, reminding Chen Guiliang that the class next door had also been dismissed.

Chen Guiliang immediately apologized and took his leave, then went to deliver Legends of the Three Kingdoms to program Class A.

The next day, these 80-plus company bosses and senior executives went to visit ByteDance and Youke. All of them registered for Xiaonei and Kaixin accounts, and with the guidance of ByteDance employees, they activated their mobile Weibo accounts on the spot.

They also followed some celebrities. Before they even left the ByteDance office, some of them had already received text messages and multimedia messages from stars. The experience was particularly novel, and they all said they would recommend it to their friends when they got back.

On the evening of the day he gave out the games, Chen Guiliang, carrying some gifts from the students, was squatting in Guanghua's Room 202, waiting for Chen Xiaoxu to appear.

A call came from Tao Chenggang's end. "A venture capital firm contacted me, saying they want to do some kind of due diligence and give Bailian Technology a valuation?"

"I'm about to do my Series B financing," Chen Guiliang said. "It's fine, just have them sign a non-disclosure agreement."

"Alright then, I'll arrange a time for them," Tao Chenggang said. He felt like he didn't have any major secrets anyway. Once the NDA was signed, it would be fine.

Chen Guiliang said, "Brother Gang, sorry to trouble you with this. Please try to cooperate with them to get it done quickly."

"Why be so formal between us? Don't worry about it. I'll hype us up big time, I guarantee they'll give us a super high valuation," Tao Chenggang said, patting his chest.

Chen Guiliang said, "Okay, I'll hang up now, Chen Xiaoxu is here."

Tao Chenggang was still holding his phone. "Who did you say is there? Get me an auto—... Hello, hello... Damn it!"

(End of Chapter)
